client: Swift ArgusNativeAuth (supabase-swift 2.55.2) XCTest hosted in ArgusAuthProbeApp on iOS Simulator
environment: Xcode 27.0; simulator 'Argus Native Auth Proof' (iPhone 17 Pro), iOS-27-0; lane stack argus-native-auth-proof
xcodebuild_summary: Executed 11 tests, with 1 failure (0 unexpected) in 36.099 (36.106) seconds

results.expected: Relaunched client restores the session from Keychain and reaches GET /me; item is device-only
results.note: Storage is the probe's KeychainStore. The SDK default KeychainLocalStorage uses AfterFirstUnlock, which migrates through backups.
results.scenario: Sign in through Argus, hand the session to supabase-swift, relaunch with a new client

results.expected: No Argus cookie stored anywhere; a request without the bearer is 401
results.note: Contrast with HTTP probe A11, where a default cookie store authenticates a bearer-less request as the previous user.
results.scenario: Argus sets sb-* cookies on sign-in; the app's transport refuses them

results.expected: One refresh (one new access token shared by all), every request 200, rotated token persisted
results.note: supabase-swift's SessionManager actor shares one in-flight refresh task.
results.scenario: Eight concurrent requests start after the access token entered its refresh margin

results.expected: 401, one refresh attempt refused, local session cleared, app shows signed out
results.scenario: Another device signs out everywhere; this device makes its next request

results.expected: Forgotten refresh token still works server-side; after sign-out both tokens are dead
results.note: supabase-swift removes the local session before the network revoke and does not retry it. An offline sign-out leaves the server session live (see report).

results.expected: Alice's late response is dropped; Alice's cache is gone; Bob sees Bob
results.note: The server cannot do this for the client. The web has the same rule in chat-request-session.ts and a known resend gap (#688).
results.scenario: Alice's request is in flight when the user switches to Bob

results.expected: Sign-in claims the guest conversation; handoff deleted; no other cookie kept
results.scenario: Guest converts to an existing account; the app keeps only the two handoff cookies in Keychain

results.expected: Claim succeeds with no cookies at all; wrong account gets wrong_destination and its session is revoked, not orphaned
results.note: Runs on the simulator, but through the synthetic adapter, so it is level 2 for the Argus contract.
results.scenario: Same conversion over the proposed header transport, plus a wrong-account sign-in

results.expected: Signup returns no session; the handoff survives relaunch in Keychain and claims on sign-in
results.scenario: Guest signs up, confirms by email outside the app, relaunches, signs in

results.expected: Only the first valid callback on the requesting device yields a session
results.note: Callback URLs are handed to the SDK in-process. Delivery of a custom-scheme URL to the app is shown separately with simctl openurl; universal links are not verified.
results.scenario: App callback handling for valid, repeated, foreign-device, forged, and expired recovery callbacks

results.expected: No access or refresh token appears in log output
results.note: Failed assumption when true. The SDK attaches the refresh token to its logger context during refresh, and Session has no redacting description. Ship with logger: nil and never interpolate Session.
results.scenario: An app passes a logger to supabase-swift, or logs a Session value
